item.text: I’m using a Galaxy user-defined tool because it can query the indexed public panel remotely and run `bcftools gtcheck` without downloading the 20 GB chromosome file. The job will rank all panel samples over the full 5 Mb window and independently over its left and right halves.

item.text: The full-window rank table is now filtered. I’m using a small Galaxy UDT to emit only the first and last five `DC` records from all three runs, so I can determine sort direction and verify the same donor wins each comparison.

representation.name: Summarize genotype concordance ranks
representation.shell_command: grep '^DC' $(inputs.full.path) | head -n 5 > summary.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.full.path) | tail -n 5 >> summary.txt && echo LEFT >> summary.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.left.path) | head -n 5 >> summary.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.left.path) | tail -n 5 >> summary.txt && echo RIGHT >> summary.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.right.path) | head -n 5 >> summary.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.right.path) | tail -n 5 >> summary.txt

item.text: The `gtcheck` records are in panel sample order, not rank order. I’ve confirmed the columns encode discordant plus matching genotypes summing to the compared-site count, so I’m sorting each Galaxy result numerically by discordant genotype count and taking the best ten.

representation.name: Rank genotype concordance by discordance
representation.shell_command: grep '^DC' $(inputs.full.path) | sort -k4,4n | head -n 10 > ranked.txt && echo LEFT >> ranked.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.left.path) | sort -k4,4n | head -n 10 >> ranked.txt && echo RIGHT >> ranked.txt && grep '^DC' $(inputs.right.path) | sort -k4,4n | head -n 10 >> ranked.txt
